title: Catalan Opening: Open Defense
line: Black takes White's side pawn, and White wins it back while the bishop watches the long diagonal.

steps.text: The Catalan, and Black's bishop comes out first. Black's pawn can still take on c4 later.
Bring the knight out, ready to castle.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
steps.after: Black takes the pawn on c4: the Open Defense. White does not hurry to take it back.

steps.text: Bring the queen out, ready to take back on c4.
steps.after: Black holds on to the pawn. The usual move is the pawn on a7 first; this lesson shows where holding on leads.

steps.text: Strike at the pawn that guards c4 with the pawn on a2.
steps.after: Black guards it again, from c7. That is the mistake, and club players often make it.

steps.text: Black slipped with the pawn on c6. Take the pawn on b5.
steps.after: Black takes back. Now look down the long diagonal.

steps.text: Jump the knight out of the bishop's way. Now the bishop attacks the rook on a8.
steps.after: Black cannot keep the rook, and White comes out ahead.

summary: When Black takes the side pawn, White castles and takes it back later. Holding on to it opens the long diagonal.
